K-381.title: Bildergeschichte ausschneiden: zuerst, dann, zum Schluss
K-381.instruction: Schneide die Bilder aus jedem Streifen aus und klebe sie an der Leine mit demselben Zeichen in die leeren Rahmen über Zuerst, Dann und Zum Schluss.

G1-400.title: Bildergeschichte: Was passiert als Nächstes?
G1-400.instruction: Schau dir die drei Bilder jeder Geschichte an und kreise darunter das Bild ein, das in den Rahmen mit dem Fragezeichen gehört.

G1-401.title: Bildergeschichte: Anfang, Mitte und Schluss
G1-401.instruction: Schau dir Anfang und Schluss jeder Geschichte an und male in den großen Rahmen in der Mitte, was dazwischen passiert.

G1-402.title: Bildergeschichte: Sätze ordnen und den Bildern zuordnen
G1-402.instruction: Nummeriere die Sätze jeder Geschichte in den Kästchen der Reihe nach und verbinde dann jeden Satz mit seinem Bild.

G2-378.title: Bildergeschichte schreiben mit Worthilfen
G2-378.instruction: Schreibe zu jedem Bild auf die Linien, was passiert, und fang mit dem Wort an, das schon auf der ersten Linie steht.

K-380.title: Gesunde Gewohnheiten: Was benutzt jedes Kind?
K-380.instruction: Zieh eine Linie von jedem Kind zu dem, was es benutzt.

K-382.title: Richtig Hände waschen
K-382.instruction: Schreibe 1 bis 5 in die Kästchen, so wie wir die Hände waschen.

G1-403.title: Zähneputzen: vorher, beim Putzen oder danach?
G1-403.instruction: Kreise bei jedem Bild ein: vorher, beim Putzen oder danach.

G1-404.title: Keime stoppen: Was hilft?
G1-404.instruction: Kreise in jeder Reihe das Bild ein, das Keime stoppt.

G2-379.title: Hygiene und Gesundheit: Warum machen wir das?
G2-379.instruction: Verbinde jede Gewohnheit mit dem Satz, der sagt, warum wir das tun.

G1-405.title: Wochenplan für gesunde Gewohnheiten zum Abhaken
G1-405.instruction: Mach jeden Tag ein Häkchen in das Kästchen für alles, was du gemacht hast.

G1-398.title: Lebensräume der Tiere: Wald, Wiese, Teich und Meer

K-383.instruction: Verbinde jedes Tier mit seinem Zuhause.

G1-406.title: Lebensraum: Welches Tier lebt hier nicht?

G1-407.title: Was brauchen Tiere? Nahrung und ein Zuhause

G2-381.title: Forscherblatt: Lebensraum Teich

G1-399.title: Schwimmen und Sinken: Versuch mit Vermutung

G1-408.title: Schwer oder leicht? Versuch zum Schwimmen und Sinken

G2-382.title: Schwimmt Knete? Versuch mit Knetkugel und Knetboot

G2-383.title: Schwimmen und Sinken: Richtig oder falsch?

enAudit: G1-398 habitats base (EN) "Look at the habitats. Under each animal, write the letter of the habitat where it lives." and G2-381 report "Draw three animals ... Write a plant ... Circle the words that fit." are two and three sentences; the brief asks for ONE child-level sentence. de writes each as one sentence.

G2-377 cursive G2-386 (EN) "Trace each grey word without lifting your pencil, then write it. Add the dots and crosses last." and G3-401 "Copy each printed sentence ... Trace the grey sentence first." are two sentences each (one-sentence rule). Also G3-401: only the FIRST sentence carries a grey model, so "Trace the grey sentence first" reads as if every item had one; de says "spure beim ersten Satz zuerst den grauen Satz nach".

G2-377 cursive (de-va font): Playwrite DE VA draws the lowercase t as a tall closed loop reaching toward the ascender line (the ribbon and the chains read like a capital "A" / "ℓ" at a glance, out/dev/G2-377-probe-de-va-d2.png). The VA t is written in one stroke without a separate crossbar, so a loop is authentic in principle, but the loop here is taller than the x-band and the chain "ttt" is hard to read; a German teacher will want a human print check of the VA t before the de base (lesson i u ü t) ships. The LA t (separate crossbar) matches what children learn.

G1-399 sink-or-float K-384 (de render): the tub tags have a FIXED width (0.28w - 20 = 159 px) with an icon, and a single long word cannot wrap: de "schwimmt" (Baloo 22) overflowed the pill, its last letter cut by the border. de switched to the clearer K pair schwimmt oben / geht unter (the gate synth uses the same pair), but the single word schwimmt (~117 px) STILL clips in the 159 px pill beside the icon, and no German float verb is shorter: the tag must widen or auto-size its word (a component fix; any locale with a long float verb clips).

G1-398 habitats heron picture (birds 2/heron): black-and-white with a red-orange beak and red legs, it reads as a STORK (Weißstorch) to a German child, not a grey heron. It only appears as a Teich resident in F2 (coastal rule keeps it off every de base page because Meer is always on the page), and storks do forage at ponds, so no second answer arises; but the landing and any caption must not call it "Reiher" with confidence.

G1-398 habitats F1 / F4 rabbit (forest creatures/rabbit): long ears, most German children say "Hase". A Feldhase does NOT dig a burrow (it lies in a Sasse); only the Kaninchen does. The page prints no words so the match still holds, but de landings and homeWord use "Kaninchenbau" and must never write "Hasenbau".

K-380 healthy-habits F2 phase chips (EN "before / during / after"): a bare "during" chip names no activity; de prints "vorher / beim Putzen / danach" so the middle chip anchors the other two ("dabei" alone was rejected for the same reason; the full "vor dem Putzen / nach dem Putzen" fit at 145.7 px but crowd the 152 px chip).

K-380 healthy-habits BASE, blow-nose plaque (read in the de render): the faceless child with the hand at the nose and a burst reads as SNEEZING INTO THE HAND. The same family's F3 teaches that coughing / sneezing goes into the elbow, and a German teacher will see the base modelling the outdated habit the sibling face forbids. Suggest the d2 contingency (blow-nose -> sun-protect) or redrawing the pose with a hand held AWAY from the face.

K-380 healthy-habits F4 wash-hands reason (EN) "It takes away the germs we picked up.": fine in English; the literal German calque "die wir angefasst haben" says we touched the germs themselves. de: "So werden die Keime weggespült, die wir von überall mitgebracht haben." (Panels should not calque "picked up".)

G1-398 habitats F5 report (EN): the hot | cold and wet | dry chips force a binary with no honest answer for a temperate forest or meadow (neither hot nor cold); de always prints Wald (sets.base[0]), so a German teacher gets a page whose own chips have no correct circle. Suggest a third neutral chip ("mild" / "mittel") or a set-dependent chip pair.

G2-377 cursive F3 G2-386 (EN) "Trace each grey word without lifting your pencil": untrue whenever the word starts with a capital that does not join (German nouns such as Tasse, Tor or Fisch: several capitals, e.g. T and F, are not joined to the next letter) and for every t cross. de says "schreibe es dann selbst verbunden" instead of promising no pen lift.

G2-377 cursive F5 G3-401 (de-va render): Playwrite DE VA sets the word space very narrow in the grey model ("rennt schnell" nearly touches), so a Klasse-3 child copying it may run words together; worth a word-spacing check in the model node (a font/space-width issue, not a string issue).

G2-377 cursive F1 G2-384 (de): the LA capitals E B M F L and the joined names Emma / Ben / Mia / Finn / Lina read as authentic Lateinische Ausgangsschrift; the de title was shortened to "Großbuchstaben in {U}" because the resolved 63-char title wrapped to FOUR lines in the narrow title column (a 4-line title is the fi-only chrome budget).

G2-377 cursive F3/F4 pictures (opened): animals/cat and animals/tiger are the same orange striped cub, drawn alike; on the F4 reading face a child matching "cat" and "tiger" (Katze / Tiger) has two defensible pictures for each word. de drops animals/tiger from its words map; the pinned list (CURSIVE_WRITING_NEUTRAL.pictures) should exclude one of the two for every locale. animals/duck is a yellow DUCKLING (a German child says "Küken"); kept because the word is printed beside it.
